coupling_convention: |d_e^(1)|, dimensionless linear scalar-photon coupling coefficient (Damour-Donoghue normalization), exactly as plotted on the log10|d_e^(1)| axis of Fig. 3 top panel
notes: Hees et al. 2018 (arXiv:1807.04512). Paper derives MRA constraints on multiple dilaton-matter couplings (d_e, d_mhat-d_g, d_me-d_g, and quadratic analogues) from Eot-Wash torsion-balance UFF tests, MICROSCOPE, and atomic clock comparisons. The exclusion curves are in Figs. 3-4, which are not numerically readable in the provided text. The emitted data points are an approximate flat (mass-independent) bound on d_g reconstructed from the paper's own formulas (Eqs. 11-12, 40) using Table I dilatonic charges and the Be-Ti Eot-Wash Eotvos measurement eta=(0.3+/-1.8)e-13 (95% CL ~3.9e-13), giving |d_g| < ~8e-6, valid for masses where the Yukawa range exceeds the Earth radius (m_phi < ~3e-14 eV) down to the paper's stated lower mass range ~1e-24 eV; the bound degrades at higher masses. Coupling type follows the ScalarBaryon hint (WEP/Eotvos test constraining d_g), but the paper equally constrains ScalarPhoton (d_e) and ScalarElectron (d_me-d_g), so the type assignment is ambiguous. Linear-coupling UFF bounds do NOT assume the field is DM, hence dm_density null (paper uses 0.4 GeV/cm^3 only for clock/oscillation and quadratic constraints).
